title: FHC Output Artifact
description: The complete, structured output of the Finding Hidden Customers agent. This is the sole accepted input to the MWR agent. FHC produces it; MWR consumes it. Neither agent contains the other. This schema is the federated boundary between them. v2.0 adds a required per-segment members roster (each account with its observed EDP value and a stamped source) and an optional resolved_conditions array, so MWR can treat a buyer claim as entailed by membership rather than asserted with an 'if'. See FHC_CONTRACT_AMENDMENT.md.

schema_version.description: Version of this contract the artifact conforms to. Pinned to 2.0: the members roster (see $defs.segment) is a breaking change, so pre-roster artifacts (schema_version 1.0, no members) fail validation loudly rather than pass quietly. Bump this const when a future breaking amendment lands.

source_agent.description: The agent and version that produced this artifact. Example: FHC v0.5 Beta

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of generation. Used by MWR to judge how fresh the underlying signals are.

brand_profile.description: MWR-CRITICAL. The vendor being sold for. MWR relates every buyer insight back to this value prop. If a field here is empty, MWR cannot satisfy Gold Standard 2 (relates to value prop).

product.description: What the vendor actually sells, in plain language.

value_prop.description: MWR-CRITICAL. The core value the vendor delivers. The anchor every message ties back to.

differentiator.description: MWR-CRITICAL. Why this vendor over alternatives. Often the sharpest hook for messaging.

buyer_titles.description: Titles of the people who buy. MWR uses these to pitch the message at the right altitude.

industry_analysis.description: CONTEXT. The regulatory and market forces behind the segmentation. MWR uses this to ground source claims, not as primary input. Optional but recommended.

macro_moment.description: One-paragraph statement of the structural shift driving demand.

segments.description: MWR-CRITICAL. The pain-qualified segments. MWR generates messaging for Gold segments by default. Each segment must carry enough structured, sourced specifics for MWR to clear all seven Gold Standards.

recommended_segment_id.description: segment_id of the segment FHC recommends leading with.

source_ref.description: A traceable source. Required wherever a factual claim is made. access_class and publisher are required so the downstream agent never infers public-ness; it reads the fields and applies mechanical checks. FHC sets these at export time, where the methodology context lives.

publisher.description: The organization that authored or maintains this source. Used to mechanically detect self-citation: a source whose publisher matches brand_profile.company may not be classed 'public'. Examples: KFF, CMS, SEC, Health Management Associates.

as_of.description: When this source was current. Free text or date. Metadata only; drives no automatic freshness rule.

access_class.description: public = third-party, neutral, independently verifiable by the buyer (government records, regulatory filings, public trackers, SEC filings). vendor_published = authored or commissioned by the seller and publicly readable (issue briefs, blog posts, the vendor's own survey writeup). proprietary = not publicly available (in-house microdata, private CRM). Only 'public' sources may satisfy Gold Standards 3, 6, and 7. A 'public' source must carry a resolvable url and must not be published by the vendor. See the MWR constitution.

specific_fact.description: A single concrete, sourced fact. This is the load-bearing unit for Gold Standard 7 (concrete and specific: names, numbers, dates, locations). FHC extracts these from its analysis so MWR does not have to re-derive them from prose and risk fabrication.

fact.description: The fact as a complete statement. Example: 43 state Medicaid agencies are subject to work requirements starting January 1, 2027.

value.description: The bare specific, isolated. Example: 43, or January 1 2027, or Nebraska.

recommended.description: True if FHC flags this segment as the lead recommendation.

pain_buyer_perspective.description: The pain in the buyer's own frame. Narrative context for MWR's tone, not its facts.

systemic_condition.description: The structural forcing function behind the pain. Distinguishes systemic from episodic.

edp.description: MWR-CRITICAL. The Existential Data Point: the single observable public signal that identifies a buyer in this segment. The seed of the information asymmetry (Gold Standard 6).

signal.description: The single observable signal. Example: state has no declared work-requirements implementation path on the KFF tracker.

specific_facts.description: MWR-CRITICAL. The concrete, sourced specifics MWR will anchor messaging to. Minimum two recommended. Without these, MWR cannot reliably clear Gold Standard 7 and should decline per its constitution.

members.description: MWR-CRITICAL. The accounts that satisfy this segment's EDP condition, each with its observed EDP value and a stamped source. This is what makes segment membership an assertable fact about each buyer. A segment without members supports no assertions and MWR must treat every buyer claim as unentailed.

name.description: The account. Example: State of Georgia Department of Community Health.

edp_value.description: This member's observed value for the segment's EDP signal. Example: No declared implementation path as of June 2026.

signals.description: Optional per-member values for the segment's resolved_conditions (see resolved_conditions). Each entry resolves one condition for this member with a stamped source.

resolved_conditions.description: Conditions beyond the EDP that FHC has resolved with per-member public signals. A condition declared here MUST have a corresponding signal entry for every member, or be marked partial with the uncovered members listed. MWR may assert a condition about a buyer only if it is the EDP or appears here with that member covered.

statement.description: The condition as an assertable sentence template. Example: exemption guidance was last published before June 1, 2026.

signal_description.description: The public signal that resolves it. Example: publication date of the state's most recent exemption guidance on its Medicaid agency site, cross-checked against Medicaid.gov SPA and waiver filings.

coverage.description: complete: every member has a signal entry. partial: uncovered_members lists the gaps and MWR treats the condition as unentailed for them.

data_sources.description: The public databases supporting this segment.

signal.description: What buying signal this source provides.

access.description: Cost and access notes. Example: Free, no login, updated monthly.

buyer_motivation.description: Why the buyer acts now. The urgency narrative.

viability_scores.description: MWR-CRITICAL for scope. value_prop_fit and observability inform whether MWR can build a clearing message. Urgency informs tone.

pvp_angle.description: FHC's drafted PVP angle for this segment. MWR treats this as a reference starting point, not a finished message. MWR's job is to turn this into messaging that clears all seven standards, or improve on it.
